updates.title: What a busier city costs
updates.content:
A player pointed out that demand upgrades can cost you trust, and they were right. Measured, buying every demand upgrade raises riders by a quarter to a third and cuts the trust rate by about a fifth, because a busier city is a bigger city and trust is paid for the share of the region you serve well. The trade is real and stays, but nothing said so.
- The demand upgrades now say it on the card, so the trade is a decision rather than a surprise
- The anonymous milestone pulse now records the shape of the network as well as the timing. Counts of stations, lines, trains, achievements and upgrades, plus coverage and the order of magnitude of money and riders. Still no identifier, no position, no save contents and no text, and Settings still turns it off

updates.title: Charter a line from the hub
updates.content:
A player at 1964 wrote that they had no idea how to satisfy the Örnsbergsgrenen or Östermalm requirements. The era names a corridor, but the card that starts it lived only in the shop, so standing at T Centralen you were offered Found a new line and nothing told you that was not the red line the plan wanted.
- A hub station now offers the charter the plan is waiting on, named, with its trust price. Take it from the station panel or from the shop, whichever you found first
- Once you take one, the panel offers the next line the plan still wants

updates.title: Tell each line how many trains it should have
updates.content:
The game used to have three opinions about where your trains belonged. It filled the emptiest line when you bought one, took from the fullest when you asked for one, and gave to the thinnest when you sent one away. Between them you could not keep a line small, and a line you emptied refilled itself the next time you bought a train. Now you say what you want and the fleet arranges itself.
- Each line in the Network panel has a number you set with plus and minus. That is how many trains that line should have
- Trains move toward your numbers as they park, at the usual depot fee, and a line set to zero stays at zero however many trains you buy
- Click the number to clear it. A line with no number keeps whatever it has and nothing is moved for you, which is how every line starts
- New trains go to the line furthest below its number, or to the emptiest line you have no number on
- A line with only one stop is never given a train any more. It cannot run a service, so trains sent there used to park forever while still costing full upkeep
- The line rows now stay on one row each at any window size instead of breaking apart, and show how often a train comes beside how many are running

updates.title: A bug round
updates.content:
A deliberate hunt through the whole game rather than a reaction to one report. The worst of these could lose a save, so it went out on its own.
- Fixed a save being retired to a fresh map when a network grew large. The check counted a station once per line calling there instead of once on the ground, so a big city with interchanges could trip it. Backups and exports failed the same way, which made it unrecoverable. They load correctly now
- Fixed the game freezing if you had a station selected and then switched save slots, reset, imported or restored
- Fixed the rush hour bonus landing on the wrong station after you built or removed a stop. The bonus now follows the station it named, or ends with it
- Fixed a demolition confirming on one station and removing another if the map changed while the dialog was open
- Fixed trains resting at a shared terminus stacking on one another, which left most of them impossible to click
- Fixed right clicking a panel button spending money and raising the browser menu
- Fixed the trust ceiling deleting trust a save already held. It stops you earning more, it never takes any
- Fixed two council decisions, One ticket every line and Automatic operation, having no effect until you next built a station
- Fixed chartering a line past the line limit
- Fixed prices quoted for ten or MAX differing by a krona from what was charged, which could leave a button looking affordable and doing nothing
- Fixed riders bound for a stop you removed being counted as delivered. They are counted as lost, which is what they are
- Fixed an express skipping a stop it was already carrying people to
- Fixed a signal failure outliving the station it broke, and still charging to repair it
- Fixed two lines being able to share a name
- Fixed the inspector charging twice if you pressed Move twice
- Fixed Escape closing the train inspector while the menu was open

updates.title: Click a train
updates.content:
Trains stop being anonymous dots this update, and the late game stops pricing them like heirlooms.
- Click any train on the map to open its inspector. It says what the train is doing, where it is heading, how full it is, and where every passenger aboard is getting off
- Trains now have permanent numbers and can be given names, the same way your lines and stations can
- Move one train to another line, or stable and wake it, from the inspector itself. The line rows still work exactly as before
- Stabled trains are not drawn on the map, so the Network panel now shows how many there are and opens one for you
- New council decision from 1975. A rolling stock programme cuts the price of a new train by 75 percent, because a city that orders by the dozen pays less than one buying a carriage at a time
- The council gained a fourth band for the decisions that belong to 1975
- Trains in an existing save are given their numbers the first time it loads. Nothing else about the save changes

updates.title: Big fleets reload intact, and shared track shows both lines
updates.content:
Reloading a save with a very large fleet could quietly drop trains. The limit behind it was written when 28 trains was the ceiling, and 0.14.0 raised that to 70.
- A save now reloads every train you own, whatever the size of the fleet
- A save that already lost trains this way gets them back the next time it loads. Nothing in the game destroys a train, so what you bought is what you are owed
- The limit is now worked out from the game's own ceiling, so it cannot fall behind a future change again
- Where two lines run the same stretch of track, both now draw side by side as touching ribbons instead of one hiding under the other. A trunk carrying two services reads as a thicker double track, which is what it is

updates.title: The west arm may wear green
updates.content:
A player screenshot showed the Västerortsbanan charter reading as a stray pale line breaking up the green trunk between T Centralen and Hötorget. It is a real second line and it was never random, but the confusion is fair. Historically that line was the green line's west arm, so now it can dress the part.
- Västerortsbanan can be recoloured like a founded line, and it alone may also wear the green of Gröna linjen. The pencil beside its name in the network panel opens the dialog
- It can take its own mint back at any time
- Röda linjen and Blå linjen keep their promised colours
- If the two stop line itself is unwanted, right click its end handle and the whole line comes down, any trains moving to your other lines. That shipped in 0.14.0 and works here too

updates.title: Many more trains
updates.content:
The most common request since launch was more trains. This update is mostly that.
- The fleet cap rises sharply. 10 trains can be bought in 1950 and each new era adds 12 slots instead of 4, up to 70 in the sandbox
- Trains past the first few cost much less than before, so filling a second and third line is a plan rather than a dream
- The upkeep curve's free allowance now grows with the era. A big late fleet pays a share of income similar to a small early one, and the bill still rewards the relief purchases
- Mothballed trains no longer raise the running cost of the active fleet. Mothballing is real relief now
- The new train card quotes what the next train will actually add to the upkeep bill at your current fleet size
- Four early achievements now grant an extra train slot each
- Some achievements now pay a one time reward in kronor or trust, and every achievement shows what it grants, in the list and on the toast
- Fixed the reported bug where only one line could be extended when several lines ended at the same station. Each line's end now gets its own handle, fanned around the shared station
- Demolishing a line down to its last stop now removes the line entirely. Its trains move to your other lines free of charge
- Rider requirements for the later eras rose to match what a larger fleet delivers. Existing saves keep exactly the goals they started with
- The trust ceiling doubled. Trust now accrues to twice what the next era asks, so an era and a hub can be paid from the same bar
- Lines you found can be recoloured. The pencil beside a line's name opens the rename dialog, and the colour swatches live there. Historic lines keep their promised colours
- Trains now wear their line's colour on the map

updates.title: Rename your stations and lines
updates.content:
A station built by accident arrived wearing a roman numeral and there was no way to change it. Now there is.
- Stations you build can be renamed. Click the pencil beside the name in the station panel
- Lines can be renamed with the pencil beside their name in the network panel
- The rename dialog has a button that brings back the given name
- Real Stockholm stations keep their real names
- Hub achievements now recognise a station by its place on the map rather than its name, so a renamed junction still counts as one station

updates.title: Running a railway now costs like one
updates.content:
Operating costs used to fade into rounding as income grew. Now they scale with ambition and can be managed.
- A large fleet costs more per train to keep in service. The first few trains are unchanged, then the rate climbs as the fleet grows
- New building. Driftcentralen above T-Centralen cuts fleet running costs by 30 percent, available from 1964 once T-Centralen stands
- New council decision. A standing maintenance contract cuts fleet running costs by 20 percent
- Vagnhallen's night stabling now saves real money on a big fleet
- The era front pages now print a kungörelse naming what the government asks before the next charter
- Existing saves keep everything they have, the new bill simply starts applying

updates.title: Groundwork for galaxy.click
updates.content:
Preparing a listing on galaxy.click, a free site for incremental games.
- The game can now run inside the galaxy.click page
- Anonymous milestone telemetry counts plays there as their own surface so pacing numbers from galaxy and from this site stay separate

updates.title: The feedback button speaks up
updates.content: - The Feedback button in the corner now wears amber and a small speech bubble, so the way to reach me is the one control that stands out. Most of what has shipped this week started as a note through it.

updates.title: Demolish a stop in the middle of a line
updates.content:
- Stations in the middle of a line can now be demolished from the station panel. The line closes the gap, and the fee is the same 100 kr the ends pay.
- Destructive actions now ask first. The dialog has a button that stops the asking for good, and Settings has a Warnings switch to bring it back.

updates.title: The era tells you how, not just what
updates.content:
A live report reached 1964 and could not find the red line, because it did not exist yet. Chartering it is a shop purchase, and nothing said so.

- When an era needs a line that has not been chartered, the aims strip now says to charter it and where the card is, instead of pointing at stakes that are not on the map yet.
- The charter card itself pulses gently once your trust can pay it, the same cue as the rest of the opening.

updates.title: The coach's third beat
updates.content: - Once your first train is running and a second one is affordable, its card in the shop pulses gently, the same cue the bell used. It stops the moment you buy.

updates.title: The opening coach follows the money
updates.content:
- The new opening cues now come in the right order. The bell pulses first, because fares fund your first build. Once your train is out and earning, the line end and the staked ring take over and show you where to build.
- Before this, the game asked for a 1785 kr build while handing you 900 kr.

updates.title: The first minute holds your hand
updates.content:
Player feedback said the opening was too quiet, and the numbers agreed.

- Until your first build, the line's working end now says what to do and the staked ring answers it. The connector between them is drawn louder and the ring is bigger.
- After your first build the departure bell pulses gently until your first train leaves.
- Both cues retire themselves the moment they are obeyed and never return.

updates.title: Overlays you can move
updates.content:
- The statistics and council overlays now drag by their title bar and resize from their corner, and they remember where you put them.
- Double click a title bar to send that overlay back to the centre.

updates.title: A founded line could retire your save
updates.content:
A serious save bug, found live and fixed within the hour.

- If you founded a new line from a Hub and the game saved before you extended it, loading that save was refused and the game started fresh. The save itself was never touched or lost. Loading now accepts a one station line, because a just founded line is exactly that.
- If a save truly cannot be read, the Saves screen now says so out loud when you click it. Before this it said nothing at all.
- If this happened to you, your city is still there. Refresh and continue.

updates.title: Save slot fixes
updates.content:
Fixes from a live report within the hour of 0.12.0 going out.

- Clicking a save now takes you straight into that network instead of bouncing back to the menu.
- Starting a new network in an empty slot now asks you to click again first, so exploring the menu can never quietly move you off your city.
- The Saves button now names the slot you are playing whenever more than one is in use.
- If a save cannot be read, the Saves screen now says so instead of doing nothing.

updates.title: The city answers back
updates.content:
The biggest update since launch. Trust now buys decisions, and the city you serve visibly grows.

- Added the council. Beat the first era and a new corner button opens a tree of decisions that trust buys outright. A decision is permanent, keeps paying its effect, and some decisions unlock others. Six decisions to start, more to come.
- Districts now fill with warm window light as they grow toward their cap. The reward for good service is a city that looks lived in.
- Added save slots. The Saves menu holds three networks side by side. Your current save is slot one and nothing moves without you asking.
- You can now add a station to the middle of a line. Hover a segment and click the ghost stop. It costs the station works alone because the tunnel is already dug.
- Added the golden train. Once a line is open it appears now and then, gliding the length of a line. Click it for a small bonus. Missing it costs nothing.
- The schematic map is now a reward for finishing the first era rather than a purchase.
- New upgrades. Längre plattformar hold more waiting passengers at every station. Vagnhallen stables the fleet overnight so trains cost less to run at night, and the hall appears at each line's home terminus with a small bar showing who is in and who is out.
- A quiet ambient bed hums under the music once sound is on. It rides the Music slider and stays far below the tracks.
- Two new achievements for the council.
- The game now reports three anonymous milestones (game started, era reached, ending seen) so balancing can follow real play instead of guesses. No identifier, no save contents. Settings has the off switch and About says exactly what is sent.

updates.title: The changelog, in the game
updates.content:
- The version number on the menu is now a button. Clicking it opens the full changelog, every release newest first.
- The notes are the same ones the update feed carries: written once, read everywhere.

updates.title: The save system, properly
updates.content:
- Saves are now written in a checksummed container, so damage is detected instead of silently starting you over. Every older save keeps loading.
- Export now downloads a .tbsave file (and still copies to the clipboard). Import accepts a file or pasted text.
- Backups now go three generations deep; Restore uses the newest one that reads.
- The game asks the browser for persistent storage, and Settings shows whether it was granted. On Safari, the .tbsave export is the reliable backup.

updates.title: Save protection
updates.content:
Hardening after a save was lost on refresh.

- If a stored save fails to load for any reason, the game now refuses to autosave over it: the file stays untouched, a notice explains, and autosave stays off until you restore, import, or deliberately start fresh.
- The game keeps a one-generation backup of your save, taken at each successful load. Settings has a Restore backup button.
- If the browser's storage errors while reading, the session runs in memory and never writes over the stored file.

updates.title: Statistics, over the map
updates.content:
- The statistics office now opens as a large overlay over the running game, from a Stats button in the map corner or from the menu. It refreshes live while open.
- Esc closes it before anything else.

updates.title: The shop reacts, and the city has a soundtrack
updates.content:
A large update to upgrades, pacing and sound.

- Upgrades can now unlock from how you play (stations built, riders carried, coverage, lines delivered), not just from the era. Locked upgrades show what unlocks them.
- The shop is grouped by category.
- New upgrades: Rulltrappor (faster boarding network-wide), Stationsvärdar (crowds give up more slowly), Reklamavtal (retail earns more), and Konst i tunnelbanan now goes three levels deep, from 1957.
- Trust accrues faster in later eras, so an established operator is not left waiting between lines. Measured: the wait before 1964 fell from over ten minutes to about three, for an aggressively hub-building player.
- The menu no longer pauses the game. Era front pages still do.
- Music: two calm lo-fi tracks by TAD (CC0, credited in About), and a Master / Music / Effects mixer in Settings.
- Achievements: 104 now, up from 81.
- Money and rider counters mark their milestones with a small beat.
- Stakes on the map now show which line they belong to, in that line's colour, and clicking one extends the right line.
- A maxed fleet card now says the cap rises next era.
- Fixed: resetting progress no longer shows the previous game's away-report.

updates.title: The city has an edge
updates.content:
Fixes from a player report.

- Fixed: a station placed too close to an unbuilt planned stop could block that stop permanently, and with it the next era. Planned stops can now always be built.
- Building is limited to 13 km from T-Centralen, which covers the whole historical network with room to spare. A late-game purchase, Regionplanen, extends the limit twice. Stations already built further out are untouched.
- The camera now stays with the city.

updates.title: Design pass, finished
updates.content:
Visual corrections, bringing 0.10's remaining surfaces onto the intended design.

- The statistics page now uses the designed graph, line table and record book.
- The clock and rush grade appear as proper chips in the HUD; the chip pulses through a peak and resolves to the grade.
- City notes and postcards use the designed toast, with a coloured rail marking the type.
- Incident markers are amber, as designed: attention, not alarm.

updates.title: Rush hours, the offices, and the platform-wall map
updates.content:
A large update focused on mid-game depth, based on the first days of feedback and a new design pass.

- Added an in-game clock. Rush hours are graded A–E on how many would-be riders you carried; a clean rush earns a little trust.
- From 1957, signals occasionally fail at a station: boarding stops until it passes, or you pay the repair crew.
- Era transitions are now newspaper front pages carrying your own network's numbers. The ending got the same treatment.
- Achievements expanded from 22 to 81, in categories, some hidden.
- New purchases: the statistics office (graphs, records, a per-line ledger), the works department (bulk station upgrades), Trafikledning (mark stops for the express to skip; trains alternate full and express, and no stop loses service), and Linjekartan (your network as a schematic diagram).
- Added sound: the dispatch bell, fare ticks, era chords. All synthesized, with an off switch in Settings.
- Occasional short notes: facts about Stockholm and postcards from riders on your network. Off switch in Settings.
- The while-you-were-away report now includes your running rate and busiest line.
- Six quiet curiosities are hidden on the map for the observant.
- Fleet cap reminder from 0.9: it rises each era; this update adds nothing you must buy to keep pace.

updates.title: The 1950 plan
updates.content:
The early game now follows the city's plan, after two days of watching new players wander and stall.

- Until the 1950 line is complete, only staked stations can be built. Finish the line and you can place your own stations anywhere, permanently.
- Advancing an era now also requires its lines fully built. Demolishing a stop on a historic line blocks the next era until it is rebuilt.
- The next staked station pulses, keeps its name visible, and draws a dashed guide from the end of the line. The NEXT panel names it.
- Completing a line now grants trust (the city repays the charter that opened it), so an active builder is not left waiting on trust between the early eras.
- Rebalanced against measurement: era 1952 asks for 20,000 riders instead of 25,000, and 1952 station upgrades go one level deeper.
- Hovering a station upgrade now explains what it does.

updates.title: Mothballed transfers and missing water zones
updates.content:
Fixes from a player report on itch.

- Mothballed trains can now be moved between lines. The transfer takes the mothballed train and reactivates it on arrival.
- Added missing no-build water zones (Årstaviken, Ulvsundasjön, Lilla Värtan, Brunnsviken, Karlbergssjön). It was possible to build stations on open water in areas the warning did not cover. Stations already built there are unaffected.

updates.title: Train management
updates.content:
Focused on the fleet, based on the first days of player feedback.

- Fixed: extending a line could permanently strand a train parked at the end of it.
- Trains can be moved between lines with the + and − buttons on each line row. If no train is idle, the transfer queues and executes when one parks. Queued transfers can be cancelled for a full refund.
- The fleet cap now grows each era (8 in 1950, up to 28 in the final era).
- Added a NEXT panel that suggests what to do next, from the first departure through each era's requirements. Can be dismissed permanently.
- Added 4 achievements.
- How to play now covers fleet management.

updates.title: Trust and upgrade ceilings
updates.content:
- Trust is now capped at the next era's requirement, and the HUD shows the cap and why accrual stopped.
- Station upgrade depth is now also capped by era, so the opening era is about building outward.
- The achievement toast is clickable and opens the achievements list.
- Added an icon key to How to play.

updates.title: Menu button and collapsible rail
updates.content:
- Added a Menu button for players who did not find Esc.
- Feedback can be sent from the menu.
- The upgrade rail can be collapsed to clear the map, and the choice is remembered.

updates.title: The economy update
updates.content:
- Added 18 achievements, each with a small permanent bonus.
- Station upgrades deepened from three flat levels to an eight-level ladder gated by station tier.
- Added retail as a third station upgrade axis.
- Rebalanced era thresholds against measured pacing.
- Old saves migrate automatically. Nothing is lost, and the game explains the changes once.
